message.reasoning: We need to answer. The question: "We're mid-rollout and I need to know urgently whether enabling SSO now will suddenly lock out everyone who hasn't been migrated yet." According to policy excerpts: enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until an admin separately turns password sign-in off, in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. So enabling SSO now will not lock out unprovisioned staff. Only when Require SSO is turned on will password sign-in be disabled. So answer: No, enabling SSO now will not lock out. Provide explanation.

function.arguments: {"message":"No, enabling SSO right now won’t lock out staff who haven’t been migrated yet. Turning on SSO just adds the SSO option; password sign‑in stays available until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and toggle “Require SSO.” Once you enable that, password sign‑in is turned off for the whole workspace in one step. So you can enable SSO now and keep the old passwords working until everyone is ready."}

arguments.message: No, enabling SSO right now won’t lock out staff who haven’t been migrated yet. Turning on SSO just adds the SSO option; password sign‑in stays available until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and toggle “Require SSO.” Once you enable that, password sign‑in is turned off for the whole workspace in one step. So you can enable SSO now and keep the old passwords working until everyone is ready.
